highlights.description: `generate --to mermaid` writes the spec as a Mermaid flowchart from the command line
`generate` quotes IDs that D2 reserves, such as `label`, `shape`, `style`, and `left`, so the diagram compiles
The documentation pages that moved in v0.4.0 redirect from their old addresses, keeping any anchor

added.description: `generate --to mermaid` writes the spec as a Mermaid flowchart, where before it was only available from Go

fixed.description: `generate`: an ID that D2 reserves, such as `label`, `shape`, `style`, `left`, `top`, or `class`, is quoted, so the diagram compiles. `layers`, `scenarios`, and `steps` define boards in D2, so a container with one of those names still cannot have edges to or from its nodes
The `generate` help said the input format is detected from the file name; the default is TOON

documentation.description: The pages that moved in v0.4.0 redirect from their old addresses, keeping any `#anchor`
Guides cover `--to mermaid` and reserved words as names
Troubleshooting entries for the two errors D2 gives for reserved words, and the Mermaid flag in the README, getting started, and the commands index

tests.description: Every word D2 reserves is checked as a node, a container, and an edge endpoint against D2's own list
Plain nodes named like a D2 board word are checked to compile, and the CLI's D2 and Mermaid output and its errors are tested

build.description: The documentation build installs from `requirements.txt` and uses mkdocs-redirects

highlights.description: `generate` writes labels that D2 reads as written, and edges between nodes in different containers now join those nodes
A diagram spec can be written as a Mermaid flowchart, with shared classes for both D2 and Mermaid
TOON output names fields by their JSON names, following toon-go v1.0 (breaking for `.toon` files written with capitalized keys)
chromedp v0.21.0 and cdproto v0.159.0, with PNG and GIF capture moved to chromedp's typed API
Documentation follows a standard layout, with user guides under `docs/guides` (breaking for links to the documentation site)

added.description: `generate`: shared `classes` for nodes, containers, and edges, written as D2 classes and Mermaid classDefs
`generate`: `Mermaid` writes a spec as a Mermaid flowchart, with containers as subgraphs
`generate`: style fields `fontColor` and `bold`
`generate`: grid spacing with `horizontalGap` and `verticalGap`, for diagrams whose edges run between grid columns

changed.description: TOON output names each field by its json tag (`version`, `viewBox`, `nodes`), following toon-go v1.0, where it wrote Go field names (`Version`, `ViewBox`, `Nodes`). A `.toon` spec written with the old capitalized names generates nothing and must be renamed to lowercase
Upgrade chromedp to v0.21.0 and cdproto to v0.159.0, and move PNG and GIF capture to chromedp's typed API

The documentation site has new URLs: guides, commands, cookbook, examples, the API reference, the lint rules, and troubleshooting moved under `guides/`, and the case study under `design/case-studies/`

fixed.description: `generate`: labels with characters D2 reads as syntax (`:`, `;`, `{`, `}`, `#`, `$`, quotes) are quoted, so the D2 compiles and the label is shown unchanged
`generate`: an edge between nodes in different containers (`a.x -> b.y`) now joins those nodes and no longer creates new top-level ones

documentation.description: Case study on fixing forward through three breaking upgrades, with how chromedp, cdproto, toon-go, and kin-openapi ship their releases
Guides updated for labels, edge paths, classes, grid spacing, Mermaid output, and the TOON key names; troubleshooting entry for `.toon` files written with capitalized keys
The generate page no longer says the input format is detected from the file name; the default is TOON

tests.description: Generated D2 is compiled with the embedded engine and every label, node, and connection is checked
Chrome rendering of an SVG to PNG is tested, and skipped when Chrome is not installed

build.description: Repair a `go.mod` that three dependency updates had left inconsistent, and bring toon-go to v1.0.1

highlights.description: New `card` command renders datasheet-style infographic cards from JSON to an animated SVG, PNG, or looping GIF
Step-sequenced flows: number the steps and timing, loop length and step badges are derived
Panels derived from PIDL protocol files, so a diagram cannot drift from its protocol
New `svg2gif` command converts any animated SVG (SMIL or CSS, including D2 animated edges) to a looping GIF

added.description: `card` package: render datasheet-style infographic cards from a JSON definition to a deterministic SVG with stable ids
Animated flow dots on edges with `forward`, `reverse`, `alternate` and `both` modes, driven by SMIL
Step scheduler: ordered steps with derived timing and loop length, plus numbered step badges on edges
Protocol-backed panels: derive a diagram from a PIDL file, with protocol order and direction checks and warnings for unverified steps
`export` package: headless Chrome capture of an SVG as PNG or animation frames, with an option to launch Chrome with `--no-sandbox`
`export.EncodeGIF`: shared-palette, no-dither GIF encoder that stores only the changed region of each frame
`export.InspectSVG`: read pixel size and loop length from an SVG, including SMIL and CSS animation durations
`card render` command: write SVG, PNG and GIF from one card definition
`svg2gif` command: convert any animated SVG, including D2 animated edges, to a looping GIF

documentation.description: Command guides for `card` and `svg2gif`, with getting started, API reference, examples index, troubleshooting and README updated
Card examples: a hand-drawn card and a card derived from a protocol file

tests.description: Unit tests for the card model, layout, flows, timing and PIDL sources, and a test that renders every example card
Tests for GIF encoding and SVG inspection

build.description: Add `github.com/chromedp/chromedp` v0.16.0 for headless Chrome capture

highlights.description: Static D2 linter with a stable rule-code registry, YAML config, and --list / --explain
New `review` command scoring layout, whitespace, legend, and hierarchy
New `compact` command that shortens long node labels behind a legend
Layout-engine-selectable rendering (Dagre / ELK) and a font-size floor

added.description: `lint` package with `corner-near`, a compiler-based check for corner-pinned elements
`text-overlap` lint check (opt-in, post-layout) for overlapping connection labels
Lint rule registry with stable `Code` identifiers plus `lint --list` and `lint --explain <code>`
`.d2vision.yaml` lint config (golangci-style): enable/disable rules, override severities, per-rule settings
`review` command: diagram quality review across layout, whitespace, legend, and hierarchy, with agent specs/skills
`compact` command: render with long node labels replaced by short numeric keys plus a legend mapping
Register the `review` and `compact` commands
`render.CompileWithLayout`: lay out with a named engine (dagre or elk) and font-size floor via `Options.FontSize`
`render` label compaction for long node labels

documentation.description: Lint Rules reference and Layout Engines guide (Dagre/ELK/TALA vs ForceAtlas2/SFDP/CoSE)
Command pages for `review`, `compact`, and expanded `lint`; v0.2.0 release notes

build.description: Add `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3` for the lint config loader

fixed.description: Resolve golangci-lint findings in the review command (tagged switch, remove dead code)

highlights.description: Complete toolkit for D2 diagram parsing, generation, and AI-assisted creation
TOON output format (default) uses ~40% fewer tokens than JSON - ideal for LLM consumption
Embedded D2 rendering engine - no separate D2 CLI installation required
Mermaid and PlantUML conversion support

added.description: Core diagram types: `Diagram`, `Node`, `Edge`, `Bounds` with full styling support
SVG parser that decodes D2's base64-encoded element IDs from CSS class names
Shape type constants: rectangle, circle, cylinder, diamond, hexagon, and more
Geometry utilities for points and bounds operations
NLP descriptions: `Describe()`, `DescribeSummary()`, `DescribeDetailed()`, `DescribeForLLM()`
Layout analysis detecting patterns (flow, hierarchical, grid) with generation hints
`format` package with TOON (default), JSON, JSON-compact, and YAML output formats
`DiagramSpec` for generating D2 code from structured specifications
`PipelineSpec` for workflow diagrams with stages, executors, swimlanes, and decision branches
Pipeline rendering modes: detailed, simple, swimlane, and decision
`render` package with embedded D2 rendering engine for SVG/PNG/PDF output
Mermaid converter: flowchart, sequence, and class diagram support
PlantUML converter: sequence, class, and component diagram support
Icon library access with 185+ D2 icons across 8 categories
Embedded JSON schemas for DiagramSpec, PipelineSpec, and SequenceSpec
`parse` command to extract structure from D2-generated SVG
`generate` command to create D2 code from specifications
`template` command with 7 patterns: network-boundary, microservices, data-flow, sequence, entity-relationship, deployment, pipeline
`learn` command to reverse engineer D2 from existing SVG
`lint` command to check D2 files for layout issues
`diff` command to compare two diagrams
`watch` command for auto-rendering D2 files on changes
`analyze` command to analyze layout characteristics
`convert` command for Mermaid/PlantUML to D2 conversion
`pipeline` command to generate workflow diagrams from PipelineSpec
`rotate` command to rotate SVG by 90° increments
`icons` command to browse/search D2 icon library

documentation.description: 7 example projects: network_clusters, microservices, data_flow, sequence, entity_relationship, deployment, pipeline
MkDocs documentation site with Material theme
Command reference for all 12 CLI commands
Cookbook with layout fundamentals, container patterns, and styling guides

tests.description: Unit tests for parser, geometry, ID encoding, NLP, and layout analysis
Test data with sample SVG files for parsing tests

build.description: GitHub Actions workflows: go-ci, go-lint, go-sast-codeql, docs, release
